requirements.product_understanding: A mobile-first booking platform that enables small clinics and service businesses in India to schedule appointments and process UPI payments online. The platform allows business owners to manage their availability, accept bookings from customers, and collect payment via UPI, all through a simple mobile interface.
users_and_use_cases: Business owner - sets up clinic profile, manages availability hours, views appointment schedules, receives UPI payments, and communicates with customers
Customer - searches for services, views clinic availability, books appointments, and makes UPI payments
functional: System shall allow business owners to create and manage clinic profiles including service offerings and availability hours
System shall enable customers to search for clinics by location or service type
System shall support appointment scheduling with real-time availability checking
System shall facilitate UPI payment processing for booked appointments
System shall send automated confirmation notifications to both business owners and customers after successful booking
System shall allow business owners to view and manage their upcoming appointments
System shall support mobile-first interface optimized for Indian smartphone users
non_functional: System shall support concurrent access by up to 100,000 monthly active users with average response time under 2 seconds
System shall maintain 99.9% availability, allowing maximum of 4.32 minutes of downtime per month
System shall process UPI payments within 5 seconds of customer confirmation
System shall support offline booking functionality for customers with intermittent connectivity
System shall be compatible with Android 6.0+ and iOS 12+ devices commonly used in India
assumptions: Business owners will have basic smartphone literacy to operate the platform
UPI payment infrastructure is stable and accessible in all target geographic regions
Average booking transaction time is less than 30 seconds including payment processing
Customer demand patterns follow typical Indian mobile usage patterns with peak hours during evenings
Business owners will not require advanced analytics or reporting features beyond basic appointment management

components.name: Clinic Management Service
components.description: Manages clinic profiles, service offerings, availability hours, and business owner information. Handles all CRUD operations for clinic data and schedules appointments based on business availability. Uses a document database optimized for flexible clinic profile structures with embedded service and availability data to support fast lookup and updates for business owners managing multiple clinics and services simultaneously. This component is the primary source of truth for clinic metadata and scheduling constraints that directly impact real-time booking decisions, ensuring that all appointment scheduling respects business availability in real-time without requiring complex coordination across multiple systems or external dependencies that could introduce latency or race conditions during high-concurrency booking scenarios where multiple customers might attempt to book the same slot simultaneously. This service is designed as a single-writer per clinic shard with optimistic locking to prevent concurrent updates from corrupting clinic availability data, ensuring that when two business owners attempt to modify overlapping time slots for the same clinic, only one succeeds and the other receives an appropriate conflict resolution response. The component processes all booking requests through a state machine that validates against current availability, handles concurrency control for slot allocation, and ensures no double-booking occurs during high-concurrency periods by using atomic claim mechanisms at the individual appointment slot level rather than relying on a single global lock that could become a bottleneck under peak load conditions. This service is designed with a horizontal scaling strategy where each clinic is its own shard to ensure that booking operations for one clinic don't impact performance of other clinics, and all availability data is cached in memory for fast access during peak booking times while maintaining consistency through cache invalidation mechanisms that trigger on any change to clinic availability or service offerings. The service also includes built-in audit trails for all business owner actions to support compliance requirements and provide a clear history of changes made to clinic profiles and scheduling information, which is particularly important for healthcare providers who may need to demonstrate adherence to regulatory requirements around patient scheduling and appointment management. This component serves as the authoritative source for all clinic-related data that customers see when searching or booking appointments, ensuring consistency across all user interfaces and preventing scenarios where a customer might see outdated availability information due to stale cache or inconsistent data sources. The service is designed with a multi-tier caching strategy using Redis clusters for fast read operations while maintaining data integrity through database transactions and consistent hashing for efficient distribution of clinics across multiple instances, allowing the system to scale horizontally as new clinics are added without requiring complex reconfiguration or downtime during peak booking periods when thousands of customers might be simultaneously checking availability and attempting to book appointments. The service also implements a background job processor that handles periodic maintenance tasks such as generating reports on booking patterns, sending automated reminders to customers about upcoming appointments, and cleaning up expired or cancelled bookings while ensuring these operations don't interfere with real-time booking processing during high-traffic periods by using separate queues and processing threads dedicated to batch operations. This component is designed to handle the specific concurrency requirements of appointment booking where multiple customers might attempt to book the same slot simultaneously, implementing a sophisticated locking mechanism that prevents race conditions while maintaining optimal performance under peak load conditions, and provides detailed logging for all booking-related activities to support troubleshooting and compliance auditing requirements. The service implements a distributed locking mechanism using Redis with TTL-based locks at the individual appointment slot level to prevent race conditions in horizontally scaled environments where requests might be routed to different instances. It also includes circuit breaker patterns to handle transient failures when the service becomes unresponsive, ensuring graceful degradation during outages while maintaining core functionality.

components.name: Booking Engine
components.description: Core component responsible for real-time appointment scheduling with availability checking. Processes booking requests concurrently, validates against clinic availability, and ensures no double-booking occurs. Implements atomic claim mechanisms at the individual appointment slot level to prevent race conditions during high-concurrency booking periods. This service is designed as a stateless microservice that can scale horizontally to handle peak booking loads of up to 100,000 monthly active users with average response times under 2 seconds, ensuring that customers don't experience delays when attempting to book appointments even during peak evening hours when demand is highest. The component uses a sophisticated concurrency control system where each appointment slot has an atomic claim mechanism that prevents two customers from simultaneously booking the same time slot, using optimistic locking with retry mechanisms to handle conflicts gracefully without requiring complex distributed transactions or global locks that could become bottlenecks during high-concurrency periods. This service implements a real-time availability checking system that validates against current clinic schedules and ensures that all bookings respect business hours and service duration constraints, preventing scenarios where customers might attempt to book appointments outside of business hours or for durations that exceed available time slots. The component also includes intelligent conflict resolution logic that handles cases where multiple customers attempt to book the same slot simultaneously, ensuring that only one booking succeeds while others receive appropriate error messages indicating the slot is no longer available. This service integrates with the Clinic Management Service through a message queue (SQS/SNS) to decouple these components and provide graceful degradation when clinic data is temporarily unavailable, ensuring that booking operations can proceed even if clinic data becomes unresponsive. The component is designed with a robust retry mechanism that handles transient failures during high-load periods while ensuring that customers don't lose their booking attempts due to temporary system issues or network interruptions, implementing exponential backoff strategies for failed booking attempts to prevent overwhelming the system during peak traffic periods. The service also implements comprehensive logging and monitoring capabilities to track booking success rates, identify performance bottlenecks, and ensure compliance with availability requirements under various load conditions, providing detailed metrics on booking processing times, concurrency levels, and error rates that help optimize system performance during high-demand periods. This service implements a circuit breaker pattern to prevent cascading failures when dependencies like the UPI gateway or database become unresponsive, ensuring graceful degradation during outages while maintaining core functionality. Additionally, it includes a retry mechanism with exponential backoff for optimistic locking conflicts that arise from concurrent booking attempts, providing robust handling of concurrency issues without requiring distributed locks. The service also implements a queuing system for booking requests to handle burst traffic patterns and reduce immediate contention on the booking process during peak hours.

components.name: UPI Payment Gateway
components.description: Handles UPI payment processing for booked appointments including initiating transactions, tracking status, and managing refunds. Integrates with Indian UPI infrastructure to process payments within 5 seconds of customer confirmation. This component is specifically designed to handle the unique requirements of UPI payments in India, including integration with multiple UPI providers to ensure maximum compatibility and reliability across different payment networks and service providers that customers might use when making appointments. The service implements a transactional payment processing system that ensures all UPI payments are completed successfully within 5 seconds of customer confirmation, using asynchronous processing patterns to handle payment verification while maintaining the booking status in real-time to prevent customers from experiencing delays or errors during the payment process. This component is designed with a robust error handling system that gracefully manages various failure scenarios including network timeouts, payment gateway unavailability, and transaction failures, ensuring that customers are notified immediately of any issues with their payment attempts and that bookings are properly managed even when payments fail. The service implements a sophisticated retry mechanism for failed UPI transactions that automatically attempts to reprocess payments using different UPI providers or alternative payment methods when initial attempts fail, reducing the likelihood of failed bookings due to temporary payment infrastructure issues. This component also includes comprehensive fraud detection capabilities that monitor for suspicious payment patterns and prevent fraudulent bookings from being processed successfully, implementing real-time risk assessment algorithms that analyze transaction data to identify potentially malicious activities while maintaining a high success rate for legitimate payments. The service maintains detailed audit trails of all payment transactions including timestamps, transaction IDs, payment statuses, and any error messages or system responses that occurred during the payment process, providing complete visibility into payment processing for compliance and troubleshooting purposes. This component is designed with high availability requirements in mind, using redundant connections to multiple UPI providers and implementing failover mechanisms that automatically switch to alternative payment channels when primary providers experience outages, ensuring that customers can always complete their payments even when individual payment gateways are unavailable during peak periods or system maintenance windows. Additionally, this service implements a multi-gateway strategy with automatic failover between multiple UPI providers, including a fallback mechanism for traditional payment methods (like bank transfers) when primary UPI infrastructure is unavailable, and includes monitoring and alerting for payment gateway performance to proactively detect and respond to infrastructure issues. The service also implements certificate pinning for all UPI gateway communications to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks and includes additional monitoring for payment gateway responses to detect any anomalies in transaction processing.

components.name: Notification Service
components.description: Sends automated confirmation notifications to both business owners and customers after successful booking. Handles SMS and email delivery for appointment confirmations, reminders, and updates. This component is designed as a high-throughput messaging service that can handle the volume of notifications required for 100,000 monthly active users while maintaining the 99.9% availability target through redundant delivery channels and robust error handling mechanisms. The service implements a multi-channel notification system that can deliver messages via SMS, email, or in-app notifications depending on user preferences and device capabilities, ensuring that all booking confirmations and updates reach customers through their preferred communication method. This component is specifically designed to handle the peak notification load during high-demand periods when thousands of customers might be booking appointments simultaneously, using asynchronous queuing mechanisms to process notifications without blocking real-time booking operations or affecting system performance during busy periods. The service implements intelligent retry logic with exponential backoff for failed delivery attempts, ensuring that important booking confirmations and reminders are delivered successfully even when individual messaging providers experience temporary outages or connectivity issues. This component also includes sophisticated message personalization capabilities that allow business owners to customize notification templates and content based on their specific needs, while maintaining a consistent user experience across all notifications sent through the platform. The service maintains detailed delivery tracking and analytics to monitor notification success rates, identify delivery failures, and optimize messaging strategies for different user segments, providing valuable insights into customer engagement patterns and communication effectiveness across various channels. The component is designed with security considerations in mind, implementing proper encryption for sensitive booking information included in notifications and ensuring that all data transmitted through the notification system complies with privacy requirements and data protection regulations applicable to healthcare services in India.

components.name: Mobile Web Application
components.description: Mobile-first web application optimized for Indian smartphone users with Android 6.0+ and iOS 12+ compatibility. Provides responsive interface for clinic search, appointment booking, and payment processing. This component is designed specifically as a progressive web application (PWA) that delivers native-like performance on mobile devices while maintaining compatibility across the range of smartphones commonly used in India, including older devices with limited processing power or memory constraints. The application implements offline booking capabilities to handle intermittent connectivity scenarios common in Indian mobile networks, storing booking requests locally and automatically synchronizing them when network connectivity is restored to ensure customers can complete their appointments even during temporary network outages. This component uses a carefully optimized frontend architecture that minimizes initial load times and ensures smooth performance on low-end devices while providing rich functionality for both business owners and customers through a streamlined user interface designed specifically for mobile touch interactions. The application includes intelligent caching strategies that prioritize frequently accessed data such as clinic listings, service information, and booking history to reduce network usage and improve response times during peak usage periods when thousands of users might be simultaneously accessing the platform. The service implements comprehensive performance monitoring to track loading times, user interaction patterns, and device compatibility issues across different smartphone models and operating systems, allowing for continuous optimization of the mobile experience based on actual usage data from Indian users. This component also includes built-in accessibility features that comply with Indian digital accessibility standards, ensuring that users with disabilities can effectively navigate and use the platform even when using assistive technologies or devices with limited functionality. The application is designed with a modular architecture that allows for easy updates and feature additions without requiring full application re-downloads, enabling rapid deployment of new functionality while maintaining consistent performance across all supported mobile platforms and device configurations. Additionally, this component implements robust conflict resolution mechanisms for local storage data synchronization upon reconnection, including rollback capabilities for failed bookings and clear user feedback about synchronization status to handle conflicts between local storage data and server-side state. The service also implements CSRF protection for all state-changing API calls with token validation at the API Gateway level and short-lived access tokens with refresh token rotation tied to device fingerprints to prevent session replay attacks.

data_models.notes: This is a document-based entity optimized for flexible clinic profiles with embedded service and availability data. The geolocation field enables location-based search functionality, while the business_hours array stores time ranges for each day of the week to support real-time availability checking. Services are embedded as objects within the clinic document to optimize read operations for complete clinic information during booking processes, reducing the need for additional database queries when customers view clinic details or check availability.

Appointment records track all booking details including time slots, service information, and payment status. The embedded time fields enable real-time availability checking and scheduling logic to prevent double-booking scenarios. Status tracking ensures proper workflow management from initial booking through completion or cancellation, while the payment_status field provides clear visibility into financial transactions associated with each appointment.

Service entities define the offerings available at each clinic, including duration and pricing information. The embedded nature of services within clinic documents allows for efficient retrieval of complete service catalogs during booking processes without requiring separate database queries. Category field supports filtering and search functionality while is_active flag enables business owners to temporarily disable services without removing them from the system.

architecture.infrastructure: The system is designed as a cloud-native architecture using containerized microservices deployed on a managed Kubernetes platform with auto-scaling capabilities to handle up to 100,000 monthly active users. All components are configured with horizontal scaling enabled to ensure performance under peak load conditions while maintaining the 99.9% availability target through redundant infrastructure and automatic failover mechanisms. The system uses a hybrid approach combining managed database services for critical data with caching layers using Redis clusters to optimize read operations and reduce database load during high-concurrency periods. Network traffic is distributed across multiple availability zones to ensure fault tolerance and maintain service availability even when individual zones experience issues, while all communication between components is secured through encrypted channels and implemented with proper circuit breaker patterns to prevent cascading failures during system stress or component outages. The infrastructure is designed with cost optimization in mind, using spot instances for non-critical workloads and implementing auto-scaling policies that adjust resource allocation based on actual demand patterns to ensure efficient use of the 25,000 INR monthly budget while meeting all performance and availability requirements.

decisions.decision: Use document database for clinic profiles and services
decisions.alternatives_considered: Relational database with normalized schema vs. Document database (MongoDB/DocumentDB)
decisions.trade_offs: Document databases provide better performance for read-heavy operations on clinic data while maintaining flexibility for evolving clinic profile structures, but introduce eventual consistency challenges for complex transactions that require multi-document updates
decisions.rationale: Clinic profiles and services are primarily accessed in read-heavy patterns during search and booking processes where performance is critical. The document model supports the flexible nature of clinic information with embedded service data, reducing query complexity and improving response times during peak booking periods when thousands of customers might be simultaneously checking clinic availability and services.

decisions.decision: Implement atomic claim mechanism for appointment slot allocation
decisions.alternatives_considered: Global lock vs. Atomic claim per slot vs. Optimistic locking with retry
decisions.trade_offs: Atomic claims prevent race conditions but require more complex implementation, while global locks create performance bottlenecks during high-concurrency booking periods
decisions.rationale: The system must support concurrent bookings from up to 100,000 monthly active users without performance degradation. Atomic claims at the individual slot level ensure no double-booking occurs while maintaining optimal performance under peak load conditions, preventing scenarios where a single global lock could become a bottleneck during high-demand periods when customers are simultaneously attempting to book appointments.

decisions.decision: Use PWA architecture for mobile web application
decisions.alternatives_considered: Native mobile apps vs. Progressive Web App vs. Responsive web design
decisions.trade_offs: PWA provides cross-platform compatibility with offline capabilities but requires more complex implementation than responsive design, while native apps require separate development and maintenance for iOS and Android platforms
decisions.rationale: The budget constraint of 25,000 INR per month necessitates a cost-effective solution that doesn't require separate native app development for both platforms. PWA architecture provides mobile-first experience with offline capabilities essential for Indian users with intermittent connectivity while maintaining performance comparable to native apps through careful optimization and service worker implementation.

decisions.decision: Implement real-time availability checking with caching
decisions.alternatives_considered: Direct database queries vs. Caching layer vs. Pre-computed availability snapshots
decisions.trade_offs: Caching improves performance but introduces complexity in cache invalidation and consistency management, while direct queries are simpler but slower under high load
decisions.rationale: To meet the 2-second average response time requirement for booking operations, caching is essential. The system uses Redis clusters for fast read operations with intelligent cache invalidation that triggers on any change to clinic availability or service offerings, ensuring customers see current availability information without compromising performance during peak booking periods.

decisions.decision: Design for horizontal scaling with microservices architecture
decisions.alternatives_considered: Monolithic vs. Microservices vs. Serverless functions
decisions.trade_offs: Microservices provide better scalability and maintainability but introduce complexity in inter-service communication, while monoliths are simpler to deploy but harder to scale independently
decisions.rationale: The system must support up to 100,000 monthly active users with predictable performance under peak loads. Microservices architecture allows independent scaling of components based on actual demand patterns, enabling efficient resource utilization within the budget constraint while maintaining the required 99.9% availability target through proper service isolation and fault tolerance mechanisms.

security_controls.threat_model_summary: A business owner could spoof another business owner's session to modify clinic profiles or availability hours; a customer could manipulate appointment booking requests to book overlapping time slots or bypass payment; a malicious actor could brute-force login credentials for business owner accounts through repeated authentication attempts; an attacker could scrape clinic data at scale using automated tools to build competitor directories; a compromised service account could be used to impersonate the system and process fraudulent UPI payments; a customer could attempt to exhaust system resources by repeatedly initiating payment transactions without completing them, leading to denial of service for legitimate bookings.
security_controls.authentication: Business owners authenticate via OAuth2 with authorization code flow + PKCE through Google Identity Platform (managed identity provider) with short-lived JWTs valid for 1 hour. Customer authentication uses a mobile app-specific token system with refresh tokens valid for 7 days, issued by the Mobile Web Application and validated at the API Gateway. All service-to-service communication uses managed service identities with short-lived tokens valid for 10 minutes, validated at the API Gateway using a custom JWT validation layer. Additionally, customer tokens are implemented with short-lived JWTs (valid for 1 hour) and refresh token rotation with a centralized Redis-based blacklist that can invalidate tokens immediately upon logout or session termination. Refresh tokens are stored securely in encrypted cookies with SameSite attributes and rotated regularly. CSRF protection is implemented for all state-changing API calls in the Mobile Web Application, including adding CSRF tokens to forms and validating them at the API Gateway level. Short-lived access tokens with refresh token rotation tied to device fingerprints or user agent strings are used to prevent session replay attacks.
security_controls.authorization: RBAC model for business owners (roles: owner, staff) with ABAC checks for resource ownership where business owners can only modify their own clinics and appointments. Customer access is limited to their own bookings and profile data. Service-to-service authorization uses role-based permissions on managed identities with least-privilege access to specific API endpoints. All authorization checks happen at the API Gateway level before routing to backend services. Additionally, explicit least-privilege policies are defined for each service identity at the IAM level, including audit logging of all access attempts and permission violations. A centralized authorization policy engine validates all inter-service requests against defined resource scopes and roles. Explicit resource ownership checks are implemented in the Clinic Management Service where each business owner can only modify their own clinics and appointments, ensuring that even if an attacker gains access to a business owner's session, they cannot modify other owners' clinics.
security_controls.iam: Services authenticate using AWS IAM roles with short-lived credentials (10 minutes) via instance metadata service, with each service having a dedicated role with minimal required permissions. Service mesh mTLS is implemented for service-to-service communication to ensure only authenticated and authorized services can communicate with each other. All service identities are managed through AWS IAM and rotated automatically by the platform. Strict mTLS certificate validation is implemented for all inter-service communication, ensuring that only services with valid certificates can communicate. Audit logging of all service-to-service calls is added to detect unauthorized access attempts and network segmentation within VPCs is implemented to isolate critical components.
security_controls.network_boundaries: All service-to-service communication is secured using mTLS with certificate validation. Network boundaries are defined using AWS VPCs with security groups that restrict traffic between services. Service mesh is used for traffic management, monitoring, and security enforcement across microservices.
security_controls.secrets_and_encryption: All sensitive data including API keys, tokens, and certificates are stored in AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store. Data at rest is encrypted using AWS KMS. All communication between services uses TLS 1.3 encryption with strong cipher suites. Field-level encryption is implemented for sensitive fields in API responses.
security_controls.abuse_prevention: Rate limiting is implemented at the API Gateway level to prevent abuse. Circuit breaker patterns are used to handle service outages gracefully. Token invalidation mechanisms are implemented upon logout from the mobile application, ensuring that refresh tokens are immediately invalidated and the centralized Redis-based blacklist is properly maintained with appropriate TTL values for token revocation.
security_controls.input_validation: All inputs are validated server-side using strict schema validation. SQL injection and XSS attacks are prevented through parameterized queries and output encoding. API endpoints validate all request parameters including UUIDs, timestamps, and numeric ranges to prevent malformed data from causing system issues.

reliability_design.scaling_strategy: The system implements horizontal scaling for the Booking Engine with auto-scaling based on CPU and memory utilization metrics. The Clinic Management Service uses a sharding strategy where each clinic is its own shard, distributed across multiple availability zones to prevent regional outages from causing complete service unavailability.
reliability_design.reliability: The system implements cross-AZ distribution of clinic shards with automatic failover between zones. Each shard is replicated across at least two availability zones to prevent regional outages from causing complete service unavailability. Automatic failover mechanisms are implemented for the warm standby strategy, ensuring that services can be restored in under 4.32 minutes without manual intervention.
reliability_design.disaster_recovery: The system implements a warm standby DR strategy with automatic failover mechanisms including automated DNS switching, load balancer updates, and service restarts. The DR plan includes specific automation for failover procedures and regular disaster recovery tests to validate the implementation.
reliability_design.observability: The system implements comprehensive monitoring with specific key metrics for each service including booking success rate, response time percentiles, error rates, cache hit ratios, and concurrency levels. Alerting thresholds are defined based on these metrics that trigger notifications when availability targets approach breach levels. Specific failure scenarios are monitored with corresponding alerting rules.

findings.issue: Customer authentication tokens are not properly scoped to specific user sessions or devices, creating a potential session hijacking vector. The refresh token rotation is tied only to device fingerprints/user agents but lacks session binding.
findings.recommendation: Implement proper session binding for customer tokens by associating refresh tokens with specific device identifiers and IP addresses during initial authentication. Add session invalidation upon device change or suspicious activity detection, and ensure that refresh tokens are rotated after each use with a hard TTL (e.g., 24 hours) to prevent long-lived token abuse.

findings.issue: The authorization model allows business owners to modify any clinic's data if they can guess or obtain the clinic ID, despite having explicit ownership checks. This creates an authorization bypass if an attacker gains access to a valid UUID for another owner's clinic.
findings.recommendation: Add mandatory resource ownership validation in all write operations (PUT/DELETE) on clinic data at the API Gateway or service level. Ensure that every request to modify a clinic must be validated against the authenticated user's ownership rights before any database operation is performed, regardless of how the clinic ID was obtained.

findings.issue: Service-to-service communication uses managed service identities with short-lived tokens (10 minutes), but there is no mechanism to detect or prevent token replay attacks in case of network interception during token refresh cycles.
findings.recommendation: Implement a nonce-based replay protection mechanism for service-to-service calls that includes a unique, time-bound nonce in each request. Alternatively, use mutual TLS with certificate pinning as an additional layer to prevent unauthorized services from impersonating legitimate ones even if they intercept tokens.

findings.issue: The design mentions field-level encryption for sensitive fields in API responses but does not specify which fields are encrypted or how the encryption keys are managed, potentially leading to exposure of PII or financial data.
findings.recommendation: Define a clear list of sensitive fields that require field-level encryption (e.g., customer contact info, payment details) and implement an automated key rotation strategy using AWS KMS. Document the encryption algorithm used and ensure all encrypted fields are consistently handled across services.

findings.issue: Rate limiting is implemented at the API Gateway level but does not differentiate between customer and business owner accounts, potentially allowing abuse from either side to affect service availability for legitimate users.
findings.recommendation: Implement tiered rate limiting that differentiates between customer and business owner accounts with varying limits (e.g., higher limit for business owners who may perform administrative tasks). Add anomaly detection to identify unusual patterns of API usage that could indicate automated abuse.

findings.issue: While server-side input validation is mentioned, there is no explicit mention of validating UPI transaction IDs or payment gateway responses for format and expected values, which could allow manipulation of payment status or bypass payment checks.
findings.recommendation: Add strict validation for all UPI-related fields including transaction IDs, reference numbers, and gateway responses to ensure they conform to known formats and ranges. Implement a signature verification mechanism for UPI gateway responses to prevent tampering with payment status updates.

findings.issue: The design lacks explicit protection against data leakage through API response structures or caching mechanisms that could expose sensitive information from embedded service objects or clinic profiles.
findings.recommendation: Implement response filtering at the API Gateway level to sanitize responses based on user roles (e.g., business owner should not see customer details in appointment listings). Add cache invalidation policies that ensure sensitive data is not cached in plain text and implement audit logging for all read operations on sensitive entities.

findings.issue: The Clinic Management Service uses a sharding strategy where each clinic is its own shard, but the design does not specify how shards are distributed across availability zones or what happens if an entire AZ becomes unavailable. This could result in complete unavailability of clinics within that zone.
findings.recommendation: Specify explicit cross-AZ distribution for clinic shards and implement automatic failover between AZs with clear RTO/RPO targets. The current warm standby DR strategy claims to restore services in under 4.32 minutes, but this assumes no AZ-level failures; add specific mitigation for AZ outages.

findings.issue: The system allows up to 4.32 minutes of downtime per month (99.9% target), but the design's RTO for failover is not explicitly defined and appears to rely on manual intervention or slow recovery mechanisms that may exceed this budget during outages.
findings.recommendation: Define a specific, measurable RTO for the warm standby failover (e.g., <5 minutes) and ensure all automated recovery procedures meet this target. The current DR plan lacks concrete timing details needed to validate it meets the availability requirement.

findings.issue: The design mentions atomic claims at individual slot level but does not specify how conflicts are resolved or what happens during high-concurrency bursts that could overwhelm the system's optimistic locking mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Implement a queue-based system for booking requests to handle burst traffic and reduce immediate contention. Add explicit retry policies with jittered exponential backoff for optimistic locking conflicts, and define thresholds for when to escalate to synchronous locking or temporary service degradation.

findings.issue: The UPI payment gateway is described as handling payments within 5 seconds but lacks details on retry mechanisms, transaction timeouts, or how it handles partial failures during payment processing.
findings.recommendation: Define specific timeout values (e.g., 30-second max for payment initiation) and implement comprehensive retry logic with idempotency checks. Include a fallback mechanism to alternative payment methods if primary UPI providers fail, ensuring that payment processing can complete within the required SLA.

findings.issue: While monitoring is mentioned, there's no specification of how the system detects or alerts on cache invalidation events during peak load or how it tracks consistency issues between database and cache layers.
findings.recommendation: Add specific metrics for cache hit/miss ratios, cache invalidation frequency, and consistency lag between database and Redis clusters. Implement alerting rules that trigger when these metrics exceed thresholds during high-concurrency periods.

findings.issue: The architecture claims to use 'atomic claim mechanisms at the individual appointment slot level' but doesn't specify how conflicts are resolved when two customers simultaneously attempt to book the same slot. The optimistic locking with retry mechanism described is insufficient for a system handling 100,000 MAU with peak booking periods - it will result in significant retry storms and degraded user experience.
findings.recommendation: Implement a proper distributed locking solution using Redis with SETNX + TTL patterns that includes automatic lock expiration and proper conflict resolution. Add a queuing mechanism at the API level to serialize booking requests for the same slot rather than relying on retries. The current approach will cause cascading failures during peak hours when thousands of customers attempt bookings simultaneously.

findings.issue: The system is described as 'horizontally scalable' but the core booking engine depends on synchronous communication with multiple components (Clinic Management Service, UPI Gateway, Notification Service) through message queues. This creates a false sense of decoupling - if any one component becomes unavailable or slow, it can bring down the entire booking flow because there's no circuit breaker pattern implemented at the API gateway level for these critical dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Implement circuit breakers and timeouts at the API Gateway level for all synchronous service calls. Add bulkhead patterns to isolate booking operations from downstream failures. The current architecture assumes that message queues will handle failures gracefully, but this is not sufficient for a system that must maintain 99.9% availability under peak load conditions.

findings.issue: The API design uses REST POST endpoints for booking operations and UPI payment processing, but the brief explicitly states 'average response time under 2 seconds' and 'process UPI payments within 5 seconds'. This is a real-time system requiring low-latency responses, yet REST POST-per-event pattern will create significant latency overhead with connection establishment, request parsing, and response serialization for each booking attempt.
findings.recommendation: Replace REST POST endpoints with gRPC streaming or WebSocket connections for booking operations. Implement a hybrid approach where initial booking requests are handled via REST but follow-up status updates use persistent connections to reduce latency. For UPI payments, implement asynchronous processing with immediate acknowledgment followed by status polling rather than synchronous wait patterns.

findings.issue: The architecture assumes that 'each clinic is its own shard' for the Clinic Management Service but doesn't account for the fact that a single business owner might manage multiple clinics. This creates an unbounded scaling problem where individual users could create arbitrarily many shards, leading to resource exhaustion and performance degradation under load.
findings.recommendation: Implement a fixed shard size policy with automatic clinic distribution across clusters based on business owner ID or geographic region. Add a service layer that can aggregate multiple clinics for a single business owner when they exceed the shard capacity threshold, rather than allowing unlimited shard creation per user.

findings.issue: The proposed architecture includes multiple Redis clusters, managed database services, Kubernetes auto-scaling, and complex monitoring infrastructure that would easily exceed the 25,000 INR monthly budget. The system is over-engineered for a 100,000 MAU system with no cost optimization strategy beyond 'spot instances' which may not be sufficient during peak load periods.
findings.recommendation: Implement a tiered caching strategy using local memory caches in addition to Redis. Reduce the number of Redis clusters from 3-4 to 1-2 with shared resources. Use serverless functions for non-critical components and implement aggressive resource pooling. Add cost monitoring dashboards that trigger alerts when spending exceeds 80% of budget.

findings.issue: The system assumes that 'business owners will have basic smartphone literacy' but the architecture requires complex UI interactions for managing clinic profiles, services, and availability. At 100,000 MAU with peak evening usage, this assumption is violated as users will likely struggle with the complexity of the interface, leading to high abandonment rates during booking.
findings.recommendation: Implement progressive disclosure patterns in the UI to simplify complex operations. Add guided workflows for business owners with step-by-step instructions. Include a simplified mobile-first interface that reduces cognitive load during peak usage times when users are likely to be in a hurry.

findings.issue: The Mobile Web Application claims to support offline booking but doesn't specify how conflicts between local and server data will be resolved. When connectivity is restored, there's no mechanism described for handling scenarios where the same slot was booked by multiple users locally before synchronization.
findings.recommendation: Implement a conflict resolution algorithm that prioritizes server-side booking decisions over local attempts. Add a 'booking conflict' notification system that alerts users when their offline booking conflicts with an online booking, requiring manual intervention or automatic rollback to prevent double-booking.

findings.issue: The architecture includes extensive security controls including service mesh mTLS, JWT rotation, device fingerprinting, and centralized token blacklisting that are overkill for a system with this scale and budget. These controls add complexity without proportional security benefits and will likely cause performance issues under peak load.
findings.recommendation: Simplify the authentication flow to use standard OAuth2 with short-lived tokens and remove device fingerprinting and refresh token rotation mechanisms that add unnecessary complexity. Use basic JWT validation instead of complex service mesh mTLS for internal communications.

Added mTLS between services to enforce service-to-service authentication. Enhanced encryption of sensitive data in transit and at rest, including field-level encryption for payment-sensitive data during processing.

components.name: Clinic Management Service
components.description: Manages clinic profiles, service offerings, availability hours, and business owner information. Handles all CRUD operations for clinic data and schedules appointments based on business availability. Uses a document database optimized for flexible clinic profile structures with embedded service and availability data to support fast lookup and updates for business owners managing multiple clinics and services simultaneously. This component is the primary source of truth for clinic metadata and scheduling constraints that directly impact real-time booking decisions, ensuring that all appointment scheduling respects business availability in real-time without requiring complex coordination across multiple systems or external dependencies that could introduce latency or race conditions during high-concurrency booking scenarios where multiple customers might attempt to book the same slot simultaneously. This service is designed as a single-writer per clinic shard with optimistic locking to prevent concurrent updates from corrupting clinic availability data, ensuring that when two business owners attempt to modify overlapping time slots for the same clinic, only one succeeds and the other receives an appropriate conflict resolution response. The component processes all booking requests through a state machine that validates against current availability, handles concurrency control for slot allocation, and ensures no double-booking occurs during high-concurrency periods by using atomic claim mechanisms at the individual appointment slot level rather than relying on a single global lock that could become a bottleneck under peak load conditions. This service is designed with a horizontal scaling strategy where each clinic is its own shard to ensure that booking operations for one clinic don't impact performance of other clinics, and all availability data is cached in memory for fast access during peak booking times while maintaining consistency through cache invalidation mechanisms that trigger on any change to clinic availability or service offerings. The service also includes built-in audit trails for all business owner actions to support compliance requirements and provide a clear history of changes made to clinic profiles and scheduling information, which is particularly important for healthcare providers who may need to demonstrate adherence to regulatory requirements around patient scheduling and appointment management. This component serves as the authoritative source for all clinic-related data that customers see when searching or booking appointments, ensuring consistency across all user interfaces and preventing scenarios where a customer might see outdated availability information due to stale cache or inconsistent data sources. The service is designed with a multi-tier caching strategy using Redis clusters for fast read operations while maintaining data integrity through database transactions and consistent hashing for efficient distribution of clinics across multiple instances, allowing the system to scale horizontally as new clinics are added without requiring complex reconfiguration or downtime during peak booking periods when thousands of customers might be simultaneously checking availability and attempting to book appointments. The service also implements a background job processor that handles periodic maintenance tasks such as generating reports on booking patterns, sending automated reminders to customers about upcoming appointments, and cleaning up expired or cancelled bookings while ensuring these operations don't interfere with real-time booking processing during high-traffic periods by using separate queues and processing threads dedicated to batch operations. This component is designed to handle the specific concurrency requirements of appointment booking where multiple customers might attempt to book the same slot simultaneously, implementing a sophisticated locking mechanism that prevents race conditions while maintaining optimal performance under peak load conditions, and provides detailed logging for all booking-related activities to support troubleshooting and compliance auditing requirements. The service implements a distributed locking mechanism using Redis with TTL-based locks at the individual appointment slot level to prevent race conditions in horizontally scaled environments where requests might be routed to different instances. It also includes circuit breaker patterns to handle transient failures when the service becomes unresponsive, ensuring graceful degradation during outages while maintaining core functionality.

components.name: Booking Engine
components.description: Core component responsible for real-time appointment scheduling with availability checking. Processes booking requests concurrently, validates against clinic availability, and ensures no double-booking occurs. Implements atomic claim mechanisms at the individual appointment slot level to prevent race conditions during high-concurrency booking periods. This service is designed as a stateless microservice that can scale horizontally to handle peak booking loads of up to 100,000 monthly active users with average response times under 2 seconds, ensuring that customers don't experience delays when attempting to book appointments even during peak evening hours when demand is highest. The component uses a sophisticated concurrency control system where each appointment slot has an atomic claim mechanism that prevents two customers from simultaneously booking the same time slot, using optimistic locking with retry mechanisms to handle conflicts gracefully without requiring complex distributed transactions or global locks that could become bottlenecks during high-concurrency periods. This service implements a real-time availability checking system that validates against current clinic schedules and ensures that all bookings respect business hours and service duration constraints, preventing scenarios where customers might attempt to book appointments outside of business hours or for durations that exceed available time slots. The component also includes intelligent conflict resolution logic that handles cases where multiple customers attempt to book the same slot simultaneously, ensuring that only one booking succeeds while others receive appropriate error messages indicating the slot is no longer available. This service integrates with the Clinic Management Service through a message queue (SQS/SNS) to decouple these components and provide graceful degradation when clinic data is temporarily unavailable, ensuring that booking operations can proceed even if clinic data becomes unresponsive. The component is designed with a robust retry mechanism that handles transient failures during high-load periods while ensuring that customers don't lose their booking attempts due to temporary system issues or network interruptions, implementing exponential backoff strategies for failed booking attempts to prevent overwhelming the system during peak traffic periods. The service also implements comprehensive logging and monitoring capabilities to track booking success rates, identify performance bottlenecks, and ensure compliance with availability requirements under various load conditions, providing detailed metrics on booking processing times, concurrency levels, and error rates that help optimize system performance during high-demand periods. This service implements a circuit breaker pattern to prevent cascading failures when dependencies like the UPI gateway or database become unresponsive, ensuring graceful degradation during outages while maintaining core functionality. Additionally, it includes a retry mechanism with exponential backoff for optimistic locking conflicts that arise from concurrent booking attempts, providing robust handling of concurrency issues without requiring distributed locks. The service also implements a queuing system for booking requests to handle burst traffic patterns and reduce immediate contention on the booking process during peak hours.

components.name: UPI Payment Gateway
components.description: Handles UPI payment processing for booked appointments including initiating transactions, tracking status, and managing refunds. Integrates with Indian UPI infrastructure to process payments within 5 seconds of customer confirmation. This component is specifically designed to handle the unique requirements of UPI payments in India, including integration with multiple UPI providers to ensure maximum compatibility and reliability across different payment networks and service providers that customers might use when making appointments. The service implements a transactional payment processing system that ensures all UPI payments are completed successfully within 5 seconds of customer confirmation, using asynchronous processing patterns to handle payment verification while maintaining the booking status in real-time to prevent customers from experiencing delays or errors during the payment process. This component is designed with a robust error handling system that gracefully manages various failure scenarios including network timeouts, payment gateway unavailability, and transaction failures, ensuring that customers are notified immediately of any issues with their payment attempts and that bookings are properly managed even when payments fail. The service implements a sophisticated retry mechanism for failed UPI transactions that automatically attempts to reprocess payments using different UPI providers or alternative payment methods when initial attempts fail, reducing the likelihood of failed bookings due to temporary payment infrastructure issues. This component also includes comprehensive fraud detection capabilities that monitor for suspicious payment patterns and prevent fraudulent bookings from being processed successfully, implementing real-time risk assessment algorithms that analyze transaction data to identify potentially malicious activities while maintaining a high success rate for legitimate payments. The service maintains detailed audit trails of all payment transactions including timestamps, transaction IDs, payment statuses, and any error messages or system responses that occurred during the payment process, providing complete visibility into payment processing for compliance and troubleshooting purposes. This component is designed with high availability requirements in mind, using redundant connections to multiple UPI providers and implementing failover mechanisms that automatically switch to alternative payment channels when primary providers experience outages, ensuring that customers can always complete their payments even when individual payment gateways are unavailable during peak periods or system maintenance windows. Additionally, this service implements a multi-gateway strategy with automatic failover between multiple UPI providers, including a fallback mechanism for traditional payment methods (like bank transfers) when primary UPI infrastructure is unavailable, and includes monitoring and alerting for payment gateway performance to proactively detect and respond to infrastructure issues. The service also implements certificate pinning for all UPI gateway communications to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks and includes additional monitoring for payment gateway responses to detect any anomalies in transaction processing.

components.name: Notification Service
components.description: Sends automated confirmation notifications to both business owners and customers after successful booking. Handles SMS and email delivery for appointment confirmations, reminders, and updates. This component is designed as a high-throughput messaging service that can handle the volume of notifications required for 100,000 monthly active users while maintaining the 99.9% availability target through redundant delivery channels and robust error handling mechanisms. The service implements a multi-channel notification system that can deliver messages via SMS, email, or in-app notifications depending on user preferences and device capabilities, ensuring that all booking confirmations and updates reach customers through their preferred communication method. This component is specifically designed to handle the peak notification load during high-demand periods when thousands of customers might be booking appointments simultaneously, using asynchronous queuing mechanisms to process notifications without blocking real-time booking operations or affecting system performance during busy periods. The service implements intelligent retry logic with exponential backoff for failed delivery attempts, ensuring that important booking confirmations and reminders are delivered successfully even when individual messaging providers experience temporary outages or connectivity issues. This component also includes sophisticated message personalization capabilities that allow business owners to customize notification templates and content based on their specific needs, while maintaining a consistent user experience across all notifications sent through the platform. The service maintains detailed delivery tracking and analytics to monitor notification success rates, identify delivery failures, and optimize messaging strategies for different user segments, providing valuable insights into customer engagement patterns and communication effectiveness across various channels. The component is designed with security considerations in mind, implementing proper encryption for sensitive booking information included in notifications and ensuring that all data transmitted through the notification system complies with privacy requirements and data protection regulations applicable to healthcare services in India.

components.name: Mobile Web Application
components.description: Mobile-first web application optimized for Indian smartphone users with Android 6.0+ and iOS 12+ compatibility. Provides responsive interface for clinic search, appointment booking, and payment processing. This component is designed specifically as a progressive web application (PWA) that delivers native-like performance on mobile devices while maintaining compatibility across the range of smartphones commonly used in India, including older devices with limited processing power or memory constraints. The application implements offline booking capabilities to handle intermittent connectivity scenarios common in Indian mobile networks, storing booking requests locally and automatically synchronizing them when network connectivity is restored to ensure customers can complete their appointments even during temporary network outages. This component uses a carefully optimized frontend architecture that minimizes initial load times and ensures smooth performance on low-end devices while providing rich functionality for both business owners and customers through a streamlined user interface designed specifically for mobile touch interactions. The application includes intelligent caching strategies that prioritize frequently accessed data such as clinic listings, service information, and booking history to reduce network usage and improve response times during peak usage periods when thousands of users might be simultaneously accessing the platform. The service implements comprehensive performance monitoring to track loading times, user interaction patterns, and device compatibility issues across different smartphone models and operating systems, allowing for continuous optimization of the mobile experience based on actual usage data from Indian users. This component also includes built-in accessibility features that comply with Indian digital accessibility standards, ensuring that users with disabilities can effectively navigate and use the platform even when using assistive technologies or devices with limited functionality. The application is designed with a modular architecture that allows for easy updates and feature additions without requiring full application re-downloads, enabling rapid deployment of new functionality while maintaining consistent performance across all supported mobile platforms and device configurations. Additionally, this component implements robust conflict resolution mechanisms for local storage data synchronization upon reconnection, including rollback capabilities for failed bookings and clear user feedback about synchronization status to handle conflicts between local storage data and server-side state. The service also implements CSRF protection for all state-changing API calls with token validation at the API Gateway level and short-lived access tokens with refresh token rotation tied to device fingerprints to prevent session replay attacks.

The embedded nature of services within clinic documents allows for efficient retrieval of complete service catalogs during booking processes without requiring separate database queries. security_controls.threat_model_summary: A business owner could spoof another business owner's session to modify clinic profiles or availability hours; a customer could manipulate appointment booking requests to book overlapping time slots or bypass payment; a malicious actor could brute-force login credentials for business owner accounts through repeated authentication attempts; an attacker could scrape clinic data at scale using automated tools to build competitor directories; a compromised service account could be used to impersonate the system and process fraudulent UPI payments; a customer could attempt to exhaust system resources by repeatedly initiating payment transactions without completing them, leading to denial of service for legitimate bookings.
security_controls.authentication: Business owners authenticate via OAuth2 with authorization code flow + PKCE through Google Identity Platform (managed identity provider) with short-lived JWTs valid for 1 hour. Customer authentication uses a mobile app-specific token system with refresh tokens valid for 7 days, issued by the Mobile Web Application and validated at the API Gateway. All service-to-service communication uses managed service identities with short-lived tokens valid for 10 minutes, validated at the API Gateway using a custom JWT validation layer. Additionally, customer tokens are implemented with short-lived JWTs (valid for 1 hour) and refresh token rotation with a centralized Redis-based blacklist that can invalidate tokens immediately upon logout or session termination. Refresh tokens are stored securely in encrypted cookies with SameSite attributes and rotated regularly. CSRF protection is implemented for all state-changing API calls in the Mobile Web Application, including adding CSRF tokens to forms and validating them at the API Gateway level. Short-lived access tokens with refresh token rotation tied to device fingerprints or user agent strings are used to prevent session replay attacks.
security_controls.authorization: RBAC model for business owners (roles: owner, staff) with ABAC checks for resource ownership where business owners can only modify their own clinics and appointments. Customer access is limited to their own bookings and profile data. Service-to-service authorization uses role-based permissions on managed identities with least-privilege access to specific API endpoints. All authorization checks happen at the API Gateway level before routing to backend services. Additionally, explicit least-privilege policies are defined for each service identity at the IAM level, including audit logging of all access attempts and permission violations. A centralized authorization policy engine validates all inter-service requests against defined resource scopes and roles. Explicit resource ownership checks are implemented in the Clinic Management Service where each business owner can only modify their own clinics and appointments, ensuring that even if an attacker gains access to a business owner's session, they cannot modify other owners' clinics.
security_controls.iam: Services authenticate using AWS IAM roles with short-lived credentials (10 minutes) via instance metadata service, with each service having a dedicated role with minimal required permissions. Service mesh mTLS is implemented for service-to-service communication to ensure only authenticated and authorized services can communicate with each other. All service identities are managed through AWS IAM and rotated automatically by the platform. Strict mTLS certificate validation is implemented for all inter-service communication, ensuring that only services with valid certificates can communicate. Audit logging of all service-to-service calls is added to detect unauthorized access attempts and network segmentation within VPCs is implemented to isolate critical components.
security_controls.network_boundaries: All service-to-service communication is secured using mTLS with certificate validation. Network boundaries are defined using AWS VPCs with security groups that restrict traffic between services. Service mesh is used for traffic management, monitoring, and security enforcement across microservices.
security_controls.secrets_and_encryption: All sensitive data including API keys, tokens, and certificates are stored in AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store. Data at rest is encrypted using AWS KMS. All communication between services uses TLS 1.3 encryption with strong cipher suites. Field-level encryption is implemented for sensitive fields in API responses.
security_controls.abuse_prevention: Rate limiting is implemented at the API Gateway level to prevent abuse. Circuit breaker patterns are used to handle service outages gracefully. Token invalidation mechanisms are implemented upon logout from the mobile application, ensuring that refresh tokens are immediately invalidated and the centralized Redis-based blacklist is properly maintained with appropriate TTL values for token revocation.
security_controls.input_validation: All inputs are validated server-side using strict schema validation. SQL injection and XSS attacks are prevented through parameterized queries and output encoding. API endpoints validate all request parameters including UUIDs, timestamps, and numeric ranges to prevent malformed data from causing system issues.

threats.issue: Customer authentication tokens are not properly scoped to specific user sessions or devices, creating a potential session hijacking vector. The refresh token rotation is tied only to device fingerprints/user agents but lacks session binding.
threats.recommendation: Implement proper session binding for customer tokens by associating refresh tokens with specific device identifiers and IP addresses during initial authentication. Add session invalidation upon device change or suspicious activity detection, and ensure that refresh tokens are rotated after each use with a hard TTL (e.g., 24 hours) to prevent long-lived token abuse.

threats.issue: The authorization model allows business owners to modify any clinic's data if they can guess or obtain the clinic ID, despite having explicit ownership checks. This creates an authorization bypass if an attacker gains access to a valid UUID for another owner's clinic.
threats.recommendation: Add mandatory resource ownership validation in all write operations (PUT/DELETE) on clinic data at the API Gateway or service level. Ensure that every request to modify a clinic must be validated against the authenticated user's ownership rights before any database operation is performed, regardless of how the clinic ID was obtained.

threats.issue: Service-to-service communication uses managed service identities with short-lived tokens (10 minutes), but there is no mechanism to detect or prevent token replay attacks in case of network interception during token refresh cycles.
threats.recommendation: Implement a nonce-based replay protection mechanism for service-to-service calls that includes a unique, time-bound nonce in each request. Alternatively, use mutual TLS with certificate pinning as an additional layer to prevent unauthorized services from impersonating legitimate ones even if they intercept tokens.

threats.issue: The design mentions field-level encryption for sensitive fields in API responses but does not specify which fields are encrypted or how the encryption keys are managed, potentially leading to exposure of PII or financial data.
threats.recommendation: Define a clear list of sensitive fields that require field-level encryption (e.g., customer contact info, payment details) and implement an automated key rotation strategy using AWS KMS. Document the encryption algorithm used and ensure all encrypted fields are consistently handled across services.

threats.issue: Rate limiting is implemented at the API Gateway level but does not differentiate between customer and business owner accounts, potentially allowing abuse from either side to affect service availability for legitimate users.
threats.recommendation: Implement tiered rate limiting that differentiates between customer and business owner accounts with varying limits (e.g., higher limit for business owners who may perform administrative tasks). Add anomaly detection to identify unusual patterns of API usage that could indicate automated abuse.

threats.issue: While server-side input validation is mentioned, there is no explicit mention of validating UPI transaction IDs or payment gateway responses for format and expected values, which could allow manipulation of payment status or bypass payment checks.
threats.recommendation: Add strict validation for all UPI-related fields including transaction IDs, reference numbers, and gateway responses to ensure they conform to known formats and ranges. Implement a signature verification mechanism for UPI gateway responses to prevent tampering with payment status updates.

threats.issue: The design lacks explicit protection against data leakage through API response structures or caching mechanisms that could expose sensitive information from embedded service objects or clinic profiles.
threats.recommendation: Implement response filtering at the API Gateway level to sanitize responses based on user roles (e.g., business owner should not see customer details in appointment listings). Add cache invalidation policies that ensure sensitive data is not cached in plain text and implement audit logging for all read operations on sensitive entities.

blueprint.infrastructure: The system is designed as a cloud-native architecture using containerized microservices deployed on a managed Kubernetes platform with auto-scaling capabilities to handle up to 100,000 monthly active users. All components are configured with horizontal scaling enabled to ensure performance under peak load conditions while maintaining the 99.9% availability target through redundant infrastructure and automatic failover mechanisms. The system uses a hybrid approach combining managed database services for critical data with caching layers using Redis clusters to optimize read operations and reduce database load during high-concurrency periods. Network traffic is distributed across multiple availability zones to ensure fault tolerance and maintain service availability even when individual zones experience issues, while all communication between components is secured through encrypted channels and implemented with proper circuit breaker patterns to prevent cascading failures during system stress or component outages. The infrastructure is designed with cost optimization in mind, using spot instances for non-critical workloads and implementing auto-scaling policies that adjust resource allocation based on actual demand patterns to ensure efficient use of the 25,000 INR monthly budget while meeting all performance and availability requirements.
blueprint.scaling_strategy: The system implements horizontal scaling for the Booking Engine with auto-scaling based on CPU and memory utilization metrics. The Clinic Management Service uses a sharding strategy where each clinic is its own shard, distributed across multiple availability zones to prevent regional outages from causing complete service unavailability.
blueprint.reliability: The system implements cross-AZ distribution of clinic shards with automatic failover between zones. Each shard is replicated across at least two availability zones to prevent regional outages from causing complete service unavailability. Automatic failover mechanisms are implemented for the warm standby strategy, ensuring that services can be restored in under 4.32 minutes without manual intervention.
blueprint.disaster_recovery: The system implements a warm standby DR strategy with automatic failover mechanisms including automated DNS switching, load balancer updates, and service restarts. The DR plan includes specific automation for failover procedures and regular disaster recovery tests to validate the implementation.
blueprint.observability: The system implements comprehensive monitoring with specific key metrics for each service including booking success rate, response time percentiles, error rates, cache hit ratios, and concurrency levels. Alerting thresholds are defined based on these metrics that trigger notifications when availability targets approach breach levels. Specific failure scenarios are monitored with corresponding alerting rules.
